correctness.rationale: On the two scalar quadratics, the SARAH recursion is exactly multiplicative: \(v_t=v_{t-1}[1-\alpha(1+\sigma_t h)]\). This gives the stated mean-square factor \(q=(1-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2h^2\) and exact stability interval. Writing \(x_t=x_0[1-\alpha\sum_{j<t}P_j]\), the condition \(q<1\) makes the product series absolutely summable in L1 and L2; the perpetuity identity gives the stated residual second moment. At \(\alpha=1\), the cumulative sign products are iid Rademachers, and the \(h=1/2\) signed binary expansion is uniform on [-1,1]. Independent finite path enumeration reproduced the multiplier second moments for several parameter choices.

originality.rationale: The defining SARAH paper proves that the recursive direction decays in a single inner loop and explicitly presents that behavior as a stability advantage; its algorithm still uses finite inner loops and outer full-gradient resets. Later work proves last-iterate convergence for finite/restarted SARAH and studies averaging/tuning. None of the inspected sources gives the almost-sure random limit of one inner loop run forever, its exact positive residual floor, or the Bernoulli-convolution/uniform slice. The audited theorem exposes a distinction not resolved by the published direction-decay theory.
residual_risks: A stochastic-recursion paper may contain the same perpetuity calculation without SARAH terminology, but no source-specific implication was found.
